Anwarul Azim Khair, Advocate-For Petitioners. 
Rafiqul Islam, Sr. Advocate—For the Respondent No. 6.
parties:
Khorshid Nayeem and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Land Appeal Board and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 9-12-2003 passed by the Full board in case No. 3 -108 of 1995 (Review) Dhaka (Annexure D), order dated 29-8-1995 passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board in case No. 3-85 of 1984 (Appeal) -Dhaka (Annexure-C) and the order dated 8-10-1989 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No9. 19 of 1987 (Annexure-A (1) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why the respondent Nos. 3-5 should not be directed to mutate the names in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 as per decree passed-in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in respect of the 7 (Seven) SA Plots measuring 5-17 acres and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts leading to the institution of the writ petition are as follows:—

That the land of Mouza- Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj, District Dhaka measuring a total area of 37.66 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot No. 560/669 originally belonged to Satinath Bandapaddhaya alias Sagar Babu. The said land was put to auction sale for arrears of rents and one Promode Bala Devi auction purchased the same. While in possession, she sold away demarcated block of land measuring 5.88 acres to Jinnatun Nessa Bibi and Kashem Ali by registered Sale Deed dated 16-5-1941 and delivered possession to them. Thereafter Jinnatun Nessa Bibi died leaving behind only son Kashem Ali and one daughter Joynab Bibi and they transferred their share of 5.88 acres to Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter, (predecessor of the petitioners) by two registered Kabalas dated 25-7-1958 and 7-8-1958. But by mistake, the relevant SA Khatian in respect of said land along with other land was wrongly recorded in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya. The predecessor of the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 110 of 1969 for correction of SA Record. Abdus Sattar Chowdhury-Respondent No. 6 claiming himself to be owner of 8.70 acres of land of aforesaid CS Plot No. 560/669 on the basis of Amal-nama dated 18th Srabon, 1350 BS on receipt of Salami and on Payment of Rs 10 as annual rent alleged to have been executed by Satinath Bandapaddhaya. Respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 in the First Court of Munsif, Dhaka on 16-12-1968 for correction of SA record under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against Pirjada Abul Kashem and Md Hasnain Siddiqui as the same was wrongly recorded in their names.

3. The predecessor of the writ petitioners having come to know about the said Miscellaneous Case filed an application on 2-8-1969 for addition of party which was kept with the record. Subsequently upon an application for amendment, Satinath BandaPaddhaya was added as Opposite Party Nos. 3 in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 by order dated 16-8-1969. Meanwhile Circle Officer (Revenue), Tejgaon, Dhaka after holding local enquiry submitted a report on 7-7-1969. The Miscellaneous Case was taken up for ex-parte hearing and petitioner-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury was examined and on the basis of the enquiry report, the learned Munsif held that the Miscellaneous Case is not maintainable and accordingly dismissed the Miscellaneous Case by Order No. XXVI dated 1-8-1970.

4. It may be mentioned that the predecessor of the petitioners did not proceed with the Miscellaneous Case No. 110 of 1969 on the expectation that the khatian would be corrected by the authority in view of the report of the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon; Dhaka dated 7-7-1969. Subsequently in the said Miscellaneous Case Abdus Sattar Chowdhury-Respondent No. 6 filed an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for vacating the dismissal order dated 1-8-1970, but the same was rejected as not maintainable by Order No. XXVIII dated 27-8-1970. Then the respondent No. 6 filed an application under Order XLVII Rule 1 read with section 114 of the Code of Civil Procedure for review of the order dated 1-8-1970 and the same was allowed by vacating the order of dismissal dated 1-8-1970 and Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was restored to its file and number by Order No. XXIX dated 29-8-1970. Subsequently the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was allowed ex-parte by order dated 2-9-1970 and the names of the Opposite-Parties were deleted and the Tahshilder was directed to insert the names of the petitioners in the SA Khatian in place of SA record owner Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

5. That the predecessors of the petitioners having come to know about the order dated 2-9-1970 passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 instituted Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in the First Court of Sub-Ordinate-Judge, Dhaka on 29-12-1970 impleading the respondent No. 6 as defendant No. 1 and others as defendants for declaration of right and title in the suit CS Khatian No. 211 CS Plot No. 564/669, of Mouza No. 278 Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj, Dhaka corresponding to RS Khatian No. 605, RS Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358 and 1365 for an area 5.17 acres out of 5.58 acres being demarcated. Since incorrect entries and non entry of the names of the plaintiffs in the said RS khatian and malafide claim of interest in the suit land by the principle defendants, a cloud was created over the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 was decreed ex-parte against the defendant No. 1 by the judgment and decree dated 26-8-1972, declaring right, title and interest of the predecessors of the petitioners in respect of 5.17acres of land in suit CS Plot 560/669. It may be noted that the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka in his report dated-74969-filed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 clearly mentioned that in the copy of Record of Right (RoR) the suit plots were recorded in RoR Khatian No. 605, and RoR Plot Numbers have been recorded in the name of Satinath l3andapaddhaya, son of Jadunath Bandapaddhaya. But the petitioner in the schedule of the Title Suit No. 270 of 1970 mistakenly mentioned Khatian No. 605 as RS Khatian and RS Plots corresponding to CS Khatian No. 21, CS Plot No. 560/669 in place of SA Khatian and SA plots.

6. Thereafter the predecessor of the petitioners on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 270 of 1970 by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 mutated their names and accordingly Mutated SA Khatian No. 605/1. Plot No. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358 and 1365 was opened in their names and they have been in continuous possession of the case land by paying rents to the government upto 1987-88. Thereafter, their names were recorded in the finally published RS Khatian No. 76 Subsequently Moqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akter sold out 5.00, acres of land to the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 and other different persons.

7. Admitting the aforesaid position of the CS Khatian No. 211 and corresponding to SA Khatian No.605 of Mouza-Tejkunipara, the respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 before the Circle Officer (CO) (Revenue), Tejgaon impleading Pirjada Abul Kashem and Md Hasnain-Siddiqui long after 17 years for Mutation and correction of records as per judgment dated 2-94970 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 and the said Miscellaneous Case was allowed ex-parte by order dated 9-1-1988 cancelling the order passed in several Mutation Miscellaneous Cases including Mutation Case No. 9 of 1977-78 filed by the predecessors of the Petitioners and directed to record the name of Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in the SA Khatian in place of SA recorded owner Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

8. Against the ex-parte order dated 9-1-1988 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka, Moqbul Ahmed, father of the petitioner No. 1, his brother Syed Ahmed and wife Khurshid Jahan Akther as SA recorded owners filed Review application in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 on 4-2-1988 for review of the ex-parte order claiming 5.17 acres on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 of the First Sub-ordinate Judge Court, Dhaka in CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot No. 560/669 corresponding to SA khatian No. 605, then Mutation SA Khatian No. 605/1, SA Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358 and 1365 which they purchased only 5.58 acres by registered Kabalas dated 25-7-1958 and 9-8-1958. It is mysterious to note how respondent No. 6 was able to pay rent after 20 years of passing of the ex-parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968. Assistant Commissioner (Land) after considering the materials on record by order dated 8-10-1989 (Annexure-A(1) to the writ petition) allowed the review application and set aside the ex-parte order dated 9-1-1988, by which several mutation Cases including Mutation Case No. 09 of 1977-78 was cancelled. Against the order of Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 8-10-1989, respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1990 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka-respondent No. 4, who by his order dated 8-3-1994 allowed the appeal and remanded the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka.

9. The Predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner No. 1, Moqbul Ahmed filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 62 of 1994 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka against the order dated 8-3-1994 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka and said appeal was dismissed by order dated 5-11-1994 and consequently the order of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka dated 8-3-1994 was affirmed. Then Moqbul Ahmed, being aggrieved by the order dated 5-11-1994 passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka, preferred an Appeal being Nathi No. 3/85/94 (Appeal) Dhaka, before the Land Appeal Board Dhaka, after hearing the parties the Chairman of the Land Appeal Board, Mr Md Enamul Haq by order dated 29-8-1995 allowed the appeal and affirmed the review order dated 8-10-1989 passed by Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 (Annexure-C to the writ petition).

10. Thereafter, the respondent No. 6 being aggrieved by the order dated 29-8-1995 passed by the Chairman of the Board filed Review application which was registered as Case No. 3-108/95 (Review), Dhaka and said case was heard by the Full Board and after hearing the parties the Full Board by order dated 9-12-2003 allowed the review Case cancelling the order dated 8-10-1989 passed by the Assistant Commission (Land), Tejgaon. The petitioners having no other adequate, efficacious remedy available against the said order dated 9-12-2003 passed by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board in Case No. 3 -108/95(Review) Dhaka, filed this writ petition and obtained the present Rule.

11. The added responded No. 6 Mintu Chowdhury son of late Abdus Sattar Chowdhury has contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition, contending, inter alia, the Abdus Sattar Chowdhury, father of the added respondent No. 6 made an order gift on 14-3-2002 in favour of his son, during his life-time and delivered possession. In recognition of the said oral gift, his father swore an Affidavit before the First Class Magistrate, Dhaka on 21-3-2002 and thereby became absolute owner in possession on the basis of the said oral gift.

12. It is stated that the predecessors-in-interest of petitioner No. 1 filed an application for Mutation of his name in respect of 5.17 acres of land of SA Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/ 1357/1358 and 1365 of Mouza Tejkunipara on the basis of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 1970. Unfortunately the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgaon Circle-Respondent No. 5 by order dated 8-10-1989 allowed mutation illegally in respect of SA khatian which is contrary to the decree passed in title Suit No. 280 of 1970. However, there cannot be any Mutation in respect of SA khatian and SA Plot on the basis of the decree in respect of RS Khatian and RS Dags unless the concerned decree in respect of RS record is amended as per law by way of review. Moreover the petitioners are not claiming that the said RS Dags are corresponding to SA Dags So the order of review dated 8-10-1989 passed by Assistant Commissioner (Land) was set aside by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka by order dated 8-3-1994 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1990 which was subsequently affirmed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner Dhaka by order dated 5-11-1994 and finally upheld by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board in Review Case No. 3-108 of 1995 by order dated 9-12-2003. Anyway such, disputed and important question of facts cannot be resolved in the writ jurisdiction. It is further asserted that respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 in the First Court of Munsif. Dhaka under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for correction of SA record after observing all legal formalities and due service of notices upon the parties concerned and after hearing, Miscellaneous Case was decided in favour of the respondent No. 6.

13. The Chairman of the Appeal Board by order dated 29-8-1995 allowed the Appeal No.3-85/94 and affirmed the review order dated 5-10-1989 passed by Assistant Commissioner (Land) in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 on an erroneous view of facts and law involved in the case, as such the Full Board on review, rectified the Mistakes by order dated 9-12-2003 in Review Case No. 3-108/95. Since the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970, the full Board sustained the Mutation of aforesaid 7 (Seven) plots measuring 5.17 acres in the name of Moqbul Ahmed. That the Full Board upheld the mutation in the name of Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in respect of 12 (Twelve) SA Plots measuring 8.70 acres land on the basis of the Judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 passed by the First Munsif Court, Dhaka. It is further stated that Mutation of 12 SA Plots in the name of respondent No. 6 Abdus Sattar Chowdhury measuring 8.70 acres are correct and it has nothing to do with the Mutation of 7 RS Plots for 5.17 acres in the name of Moqbul Ahmed. The writ petitioner never claimed that those RS Plots are corresponding to SA Plots and, as such, the petitioner is not entitled to get any relief in the writ petition on such disputed question of facts. So the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs.

14.  The added respondent No. 6 also filed two Supplementary-Affidavits-in-Opposition dated 11-11-2009 and 18-5-2010 stating that the writ petitioner while admitting the identity of the concerned Rs Khatian and plot on the basis of the alleged report of Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka, where he identified the khatian and plot as RS. Such facts cannot be resolved in writ jurisdiction by passing the statutory provision of law. The decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 filed by the writ petitioner cannot be amended or corrected in writ jurisdiction. Respondent No. 6 in his Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition filed on 11-11-2009 stated that by Annexure-I to the Affidavit-in-Reply, the writ petitioners want to introduce new facts with a design to create confusion and to make complication as if the writ petitioners have been seeking relief in a court of appeal or revision and the same does not deserve any consideration. But in the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition filed on 18-5-2010 he further stated that Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006 (Annexure-I to the Affidavit-in-Reply) was not filed by Abdus Sattar Chowdhury which was a collusive one.

15. Mr Anwarul Azim Khair, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the "Full Board" of the Land Appeal Board was constituted to exercise its review jurisdiction conferred by the statute to review the order passed by the "Board" that is, the order passed by the Chairman of the Board, as the review jurisdiction to interfere with the order of Board is very limited. Any person feeling aggrieved by the order of the Board on account of some glaring mistake or error apparent on the face the record or where it requires interpretation of law in view of any legal complicacy can invoke the review jurisdiction of the Full Board. But in the present case, the Full Board granted review without discovery of any new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge, or could not be produced by respondent No. 6 when order was made and strict proof of such allegations or some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, exceeded its jurisdiction in setting asiding the order passed by the Board, and therefore, the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority.

16. He next submits that the order of review passed by the Full Board is inconsistent and contradictory in that the same was passed in violation of the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970. He finally submits that the revenue officers and the Board erred in law in not considering that all the 12 plots of respondent No. 6 and 7 plots measuring 5.17 acres of Moqbul Ahmed and other are related to same SA Plots and Khatian and on such finding Full Board ought to have rejected the review application.

17. On the other hand, Mr Md Rafiqul Islam the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 6 submits that the impugned order of review passed by the. Full Board of land Appeal Board in review case is consistent and as per judgment passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 and, as such, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed. He further submits that the judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 by the learned Munsif, Dhaka in respect of 8.70 acres land of 12 SA Dags under SA Khatian No. 605 of Mouza Tejkunipara in the name of respondent No. 6 but it has nothing to do with 7 RS Dags of RS Khatian No. 605 measuring 5.17 acres of the same Mouza in the name Moqbul Ahmed and other as per Decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 and those RS plots are not related to SA plots and, as such, the petitioner is not entitled to get any relief in this writ petition. He next submits that the writ petition involves disputed questions of facts which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction.

18. He finally submits that the High Court Division while exercising jurisdiction under article 102(2) of the constitution in respect of Judgment of a tribunal or in other words exercises its jurisdiction in certiorari cannot sit over as the court of Appeal. Since the impugned order of review passed by the Full Board is based on documentary evidence, the High Court Division in its extraordinary jurisdiction under article 102 of the constitution cannot interfere with the finding of the Full Board and, as such, the writ is not maintainable and the same is liable to be dismissed with costs.

19. In Support of his arguments learned Advocate for the respondent No. 6 Mr Rafiqul Islam relies on the decisions of 47 DLR (AD) 9, 50 DLR (AD) 213, 8 MLR (AD) 149 = 7 BLC (AD) 119 and 10 MLR (AD) 337 = 57 DLR (AD) 167.

20. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the writ petition, Affidavit-in-Opposition, Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition and Affidavit-in-Reply and the relevant Annexures annexed thereto.

21. Admittedly, this Writ Petition is in the nature of a Writ of Certiorari. The scope of a Writ of Certiorari is very limited. In this connection, a reference may be made to the decision in the case of the Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil reported in 15 BLD (AD) 175 = 49 DLR (AD) 26. In that decision, it has been held in unmistakable terms that the High Court Division exercising power under article 102 of the Constitution does not work as a Court of Appeal and, as such, it is not required to make determination of facts on its own. It can interfere with the findings of Court of facts under its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under article 102 only if it can be shown that the Court has acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence/facts causing prejudice to the petitioner or it has acted malafide or in violation of the principle of natural justice. While considering the merit of the instant Rule, the above 'ratio' enunciated by the Appellate Division should be kept in view.

22. No let us examine whether the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board have exceeded its jurisdiction or it has acted mala fide causing prejudice to the petitioner.

23. There is no dispute rather it is admitted that the case land of Mouza Tejkunipara Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj appertaining to CS Khatian No. 211 CS Plot No. 560/669 measuring area of 37.66 acres originally belonged to Satinath Bandapaddhaya and it is not also disputed that CS plot No. 560/669 is corresponding to SA Khatian No.605 and the same was recorded in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya. It is also undisputed that the Mouza Tejkunipara is now known as Mouza- Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka.

24. It is the case of the petitioners that the case property was sold in auction in certificate case No. 131/1930-31 and Promode Bala wife of Satinath Bandapaddhaya auction-Purchased through Boinama and entered into possession of the case property by Writ of Delivery of possession. Predecessor of petitioner No. 1, Moqbul Ahmad and others purchased 5.58 acres of case land from their vendors Kashem Ali and Joynab Bibi by two registered kabala dated 25-7-1958 and 7-8-1958. On the other hand, respondent No. 6 claimed that Satinath Bandapaddhaya Settled 8.70 acres with respondent No. 6 in CS Plot No. 560/669 by executing an unregistered Amalnama dated 18th Sraban 1350 BS on receipt of Salami and on payment of RS 10 as annual rent.

25. It appears from Annexure-F to the Affidavit-in-reply that respondent No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 before the Court of First Munsif, Dhaka under section 143A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on 16-12-1968 against Pirjada Abul Kashem and Mohammad Hasnain Siddiqui for correction of SA record as the same was wrongly recorded in their names. It also transpires from the order sheet of Miscellaneous case No. 355 of 1968 (Annexure-F (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply) that on the prayer of the petitioner, Satinath Bandapaddhaya Son of late Jadunath Bandapaddhaya was added as opposite party No. 3 by order dated 16-8-1969. In the said Miscellaneous Case predecessor of the present petitioner No.1 Moqbul Ahmad, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akther filed an application on 2-8-1969 under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for adding them as opposite parties but the same was kept in the record.

26. It further transpires that initially Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was dismissed ex-parte by order dated 1-8-1970. The petitioner-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury filed a petition under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 25-8-1970 for vacating the order of dismissal dated 1-8-1970 but same was rejected on 27-8-1970. Against the said order of dismissal dated 1-8-1970, the respondent No. 6 filed a review application under section 114 read with Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 27-8-1970 and the same was allowed ex-parte on 29-8-1970 and Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was restored to its file and number. Thereafter, Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 was allowed ex-parte by order dated 2-9-1970 and order was passed to delete the names of the opposite parties from case SA Khatian and incorporate the name of the petitioner-respondent No. 6 in the SA khatian.

27. It further appears from Annexure-1 to the Affidavit-in-Opposite that predecessor of the writ petitioner, Moqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akther wife of Moqbul Ahmed instituted Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 in the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the respondent No. 6 as defendant No. 1 and others as principal defendants for declaration of title in the suit CS khatian 211 CS Plot No. 560/669 of Mouza Tejkunipara corresponding to RS Khatian No. 650 and RS Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/ 1358 and 1365 for 5.17 acres out of 5.58 acres being demarcated.

28. It further appears from Annexure F-2 to the Affidavit-in-Reply that Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka submitted his report dated 7-7-169 wherein it was clearly mentioned that the plot index of record of right, that is ROR, the suit plots were recorded in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya son of jadunath Bandapaddhaya as ROR plot Nos. 1353, 1354, 1355, 1356, 1365, 1384 and 1385. It may be noted that this ROR relates to SA record and not RS record and there is no question of recording any land as RS Khatian and RS Plots in the year 1969 when there was no existence of any RS Record during those period, such bona fide mistake was committed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) by wrongly stating RS plot in place of SA plot. It is pertinent to note that in the Dhaka District RS Khatian was Finally Published under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the year 1985 or thereabout.

29. It is further evident from Annexure-G to the Affidavit-in-Reply that the names of predecessors of the petitioners, Moqbul Ahmad, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akther wife of Moqbul Ahmad were mutated vide Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and accordingly mutated SA Khatian No. 605/1 Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358 was recorded correctly in their names for an area 5.17 acres only. It also appears from Annexure G-1 to the Affidavit-in-Reply that subsequently RS Khatian No. 76 of Mouza Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka, Previously Tejkunipara, PS Tejgaon, Previously Keranigonj was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the names of the aforesaid persons Correctly and till today the respondent No. 6 did not take any steps in respect of Final Publication of RS Khatian No. 76 in the name of the petitioners' predecessor. Since the later record of rights, that is, RS record was finally published in the names of the predecessors of the petitioners, such entry in a record of rights shall be presumed to be correctly unless it is proved by evidence to be incorrect and latest RS record of rights shall prevail over the earlier SA record unless the contrary is proved.

30. It further appears from Annexure-H to the Affidavit-in-Reply that the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 filed by the respondent No. 6 through his Constituted Attorney, Mr Azharul Islam by Registered Irrevocable Power of Attorney dated 24-10-1985 before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka against Pirjada Abul Kashem had Md Hasnain Siddiqui for mutation and correction of the SA record as per judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 wherein the land described in the schedule of the said application is of CS Khatian No. 211, Plot No. 560/669 corresponding to SA Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358/1365/1370/1377/1383/1384 and 1385 total area 8.70 of Mouza Tejkunipara, at present Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka, District-Dhaka.

31. It further appears from Annexure-H (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply that Assistant Com-missioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle by order dated 9-1-1988 allowed the said Miscellaneous Case and cancelled the Mutated SA khatian in the name of the predecessors of the petitioner No. 1, Moqbul Ahmed and several persons on the finding that since the petitioner, Abdus Sattar Chowdhury-decree-holder acquired title on the basis of the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 355 of 1968 for 12 SA Plots, he directed the respective Tahshilder to make necessary correction in SA record in the name of Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in place of SA recorded owner Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

32. Let us first consider the relevant provision of Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy act 1950 under which the respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 for correction of SA record. Section 143A was inserted after Section 143 by East Pakistan Ordinance No. VIII of 1967. It was however, omitted after few years by ordinance No. LXIV of 1975. So Section 143A provides for an alternative right to right to file a case before the Civil Court for correction of bona fide mistakes of the record of rights.

33. The omitted Section 143A runs as follows:

"Special provisions for correcting mistakes in the record of rights:—

(1) Any person aggrieved by an entry or omission of entry in the record-of-rights prepared or revised and finally published under Chapter IV may, not withstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, file an application along with necessary requisites, for the purpose of correction of mistakes in such record of rights in the civil court which would have jurisdiction to entertain a suit for possession of the land to which such entry relates or in respect of which such omission was made.

(2) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to be a plaint and order passed thereon shall have the force of a decree under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).

(3) An application filed under sub-section (1) shall contain full particulars of persons likely to be affected by an order on such application and shall also contain the full particulars of the holding to which the entry relates or in respect of which the omission complained of was made.

(4) The court shall, for the purpose of disposal of application filed under sub-section (1), follow the following procedure, namely:

(a) The court shall cause notice to be observed on the persons named in the application in the manner as provided in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).

(b) The court shall, within seven days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), send a copy thereof, by registered post at the cost of applicants to the Revenue-Officer concerned for holding a local inquiry, in presence of the parties concerned, on the subject matter of the application and the Revenue-Officer shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of the copy, hold inquiry and submit the report to the court.

(c) The court may allow such reasonable time as it may think fit to file objection to the inquiry report referred to in clause (b) and, (3)of no appearance is made by the opposite party within the time mentioned in the notice, and if no objection is filed to the inquiry report within the time so allowed, the court may proceed ex-parte with disposal of the application after taking into consideration the said report and other material evidence on record; and (d) where the report referred to in clause (b) is not submitted, or where objection referred to in clause (c) is filed, the court shall fix a date for hearing and on that date, after hearing the parties and taking into consideration the report, if any, and other evidence which may be adduced by the parties in this behalf, shall pass such order as it may think just and proper.

(5) Any person, whose interest has been affected by reason of any entry or omission in the record of rights, referred to in sub-section (1), may, within fourteen days of the filing of an application under sub-section (1), appear to be added as co-application.

(6) The Revenue-Officer shall, for the purpose of an inquiry under sub-section (4), have the same power as vested in a civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), including the power of:

(a) Enforcing attendance of any person, and examining him on oath; and

(b) Compelling the production of any document.

(7) Within thirty days from the date of an order under sub-section (4), an application from that order shall lie to the district Judge who may, either himself hear the appeal or transfer it to any other court subordinate to him but not below the rank of Subordinate Judge for hearing.

(8) Decision under sub-section (4) if no appeal is preferred from it, or under sub-section (7), shall be final and conclusive.

(9) Where the court passes an order sub-section (4), or sub-section (7), revising the entries or rectifying the omission complained of under sub-section (1), it shall notify the same to the Collector and the collector shall correct the record-or-rights accordingly.

(10) Any person interested may produce a certified copy of the orders referred to in sub-section (4) or sub-section (7) to the Revenue-Officer and the Revenue-Officer shall make such alterations in the record-of-rights as may be necessary to give effect to such orders.

(11) The record-of-rights corrected under sub-section (9) or sub-section (10) shall be deemed to have been prepared and finally published under Chapter IV of this Act.

(12) An application under sub-section (1) or memorandum of an appeal under sub-section (7) shall, not withstanding anything contained in the Court-Fees Act, 1870, (Act VII of 1870), bear a fixed court fee of rupee one.

(13) For the purpose of an application, appeal, review, revision and consequence of non-appearance, relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), shall mutatis mutandis apply."

34. Now let us see whether the order passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 passed by the learned Munsif, First Court Dhaka was in accordance with relevant provision of section 143A the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

35. We have already seen from the order sheet of the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 (Annexure-F (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply) that the Miscellaneous Case was filed by the respondent No. 6 for correction of the SA record. It appears from the said Annexure that initially Miscellaneous Case was dismissed ex-parte by order dated 1-8-1970 and thereafter the petitioner filed an application under section 151 for rejecting the order passed on 1-8-1970 and the learned Munsif by order dated 27-8-1970 rejected the application under section 151. Against the order of ex-parte dismissal dated 1-8-1970 passed in the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968, the petitioner filed an application under Section 114 read with Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 27-8-1970 for review of the order. It transpires that without issuing any notice to the opposite parties just after two days, which is on 29-8-1970 the learned Munsif allowed the said review application. Thereafter the said Miscellaneous Case was taken up for ex-parte hearing on 2-9-1970 just after 3 days and PW1 Abdus Sattar Chowdhury was examined and the learned Munsif again allowed the Miscellaneous Case ex-parte and passed order to delete the names of the opposite parties from the case SA khatian and insert the name of the respondent No. 6 therein.

36. Thus it is evident that the ex-parte order passed in Miscellaneous Case for deleting names of opposite-parties and recording the respondent No. 6's name in the case SA Khatian without serving any notice upon the opposite parties as per law and without impleading the heirs of the predecessors of the petitioners, Moqbul Ahmed and others cannot be binding upon them and the said order is of no avail to the respondent No. 6. Moreover, Sub-section 13 of section 143A of the State acquisition and Tenancy Act clearly provides that the relevant provision of the Civil Procedure Code, that is, order XLVII shall be applicable for the purpose of filing an application for review. Sub rule 4(2) of order XLVII provides that the no application for review shall be granted unless notice of the application has been served upon the Opposite-Party and discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be adduced by him when the order was passed, without strict proof of such allegations. In the present case Miscellaneous Case was allowed ex-parte by the learned Munsif without complying with the mandatory provision of Sub-Section 13 of Section 143A.

37. Mutation proceedings are done under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SAT Act) and the Rules framed there under. Section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides, inter alia, that the record of rights prepared or revised shall be maintained upto-date in the prescribed manner under part IV, or under Chapter XVII by correcting clerical mistakes and, by incorporating the changes of account of (a) the mutation of names as a result of transfer or inheritance, Chapter VI of the Tenancy Rules, 1995 consists of rules 22-25 of which rules 22-24 relate to mutation proceedings.

38. Section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is attracted only when a person aggrieved by wrong entry in the record of rights finally published and for correcting mistakes in the record of rights on the basis of the possession of the parties in the case land in the Civil Court. This section is not attracted when the record of right is to be corrected after a finding to be given as to the title of the holders or challengers. An application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not a suit for declaration of title but is a proceeding for rectification of mistakes in the record of right prepared on the basis of the possession of the parties in the land in question. This section is only concerned with the question of possession of the land and question of title to the land is beyond the scope of this section.

39. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the cases of Assistant Custodian Enemy Property (Land Appeal Board) Tanga vs Bholanath Guha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 79 Reazuddin vs Jatindra Kishore reported in 37 DLR (AD) 202.

40. From a plain reading of the above provision of law and the decisions cited above, it is clear that section 143A is meant for a limited purpose for correction of the record of rights of the basis of possession of the parties in the case land. The respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 not only for correction of mistakes in the SA Khatian but for some other reasons.

41. In the unreported decision of the Appellate Division is the case of Bangladesh and others vs Mariam Khatun and others (Civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972), the fact are that the respondent who, along with others took settlement of land from Zamindars and were in possession thereof, challenged the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelling the names of the respondent and his co-sharers from the record of rights which were recorded in the name of the then Province of East Pakistan. By four different orders from 1960 to 1963 the Revenue Settlement Officer corrected the record of rights and inserted the names of the respondent and his co-sharers in the disputed Khatian. The Deputy Commissioner of Faridpur purchased some of the land in dispute from the respondent in 1964, but on 17-10-1966 the respondent and his co sharers were served with notice to show cause why the record of rights shall not be changed in favour of the Province of East Pakistan. The respondent showed cause but the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Faridpur cancelled the names of the respondent and his co-sharers by order dated 13-7-1967 and inserted the name of the Province of East Pakistan in respect of the disputed khatian. The case of the Province of East Pakistan was that the names of the respondent and his co-sharers were recorded as a result of fraudulent transaction between the respondent and his co-sharers on the one hand and some of the revenue authorities on the other hand.

42. The Appellate Division quoted with approval the judgment of the then Dhaka High Court in Writ Petition No. 386 of 1967 arising out of the above proceeding as follows :—

"The scope of section 143 of the Act is, is our opinion, of a very limited nature. It authorizes the Collector to maintain up to date record of rights and to make such correction as occurred as a result of bona fide mistake committed in preparing the record of rights. It does not, in our opinion, authorize Collector to correct the record-of-rights which affects the question of title or possession relating to disputed question of fact. Bona fide mistake, as contemplated under section 143 of the Act, in our opinion, relates to the mistake of the nature where a mistake has crept in which is not supported by the records or where there has been a mistake in recording quantum of the land which again is no supported by facts but where name of a person stands recorded and another person challenges that such entry cannot be said to have been made as a result of bona fide mistake, and that cannot be corrected by the Collector under section 143 of the Act."

43. The Appellate Division was unable to find fault with or take exception to the views so expressed. The Appellate Division held that the facts which were required to be determined prior to correcting the record-of-rights by a proceeding under section 143 of the Act involved the examination of documents of title relating to the lands in dispute, commission of fraud, if any, and the interpretation of various sections of the Act. The summary method under section 143 cannot be strained to consider question relating of such facts.

44. In the present case also the questions, for example, whether Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jaban Akhter, predecessors of the petitioners by two registered kabalas dated 25-3-1958 and 7-8-1958 purchased 5.58 acres. Whether the respondent No. 6 was possessing the remaining 8.70 through unregistered Amalnama and if so under what title, whether the unregistered Amalnama date 18th Sraban, 1350 BS created any title in favour of the respondent No. 6 and other questions can be determined only after examining witnesses and documents in a full-scale title suit. None of these things can conveniently or even suitable by done by the Collector under the terms and provisions of aforesaid section 143, as it now stands. If "bona fide mistake" was not covered by the facts disclosed in the aforesaid civil Appeal No. 8 of 1972, we fail to see how "clerical mistake" can be found in the present case.

45. We have already seen that the predecessors of the petitioners acquired title in the case property on the basis of the decree dated 29-12-1970 passed in Title Suit No. 240 of 1970 against the respondent No. 6 and others.

46. We have also seen that on the basis of an ex-parte order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 355 of 1968 the respondent No. 6 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon, Dhaka (Annexure-H to the Affidavit-in-Reply) for mutation and correction of the SA record long after 17 years without impleading Moqbul Ahmed and others, predecessor of the writ petitioner and when the name of Satinath was recorded in the finally published SA Khatian No. 605. It appears that long before filing of the said Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 the Circle Officer (Revenue) Tejgaon opened mutated SA Khatian No. 605/1 of Mouza Tejkunipara in the name of Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Mrs Khurshid Jahan Akhter in Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and they have been possessing the same by paying rents to the Government regularly. But the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle Dhaka by order dated 9-1-1988 Passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 erroneously cancelled several Mutation cases including the Mutation Case No. 9 of 1977 filed by the petitioners predecessors, Moqbul Ahmed and others. Thus the order of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 9-1-1988 is not operative against the predecessors of the petitioners who were admittedly not parties to the Mutation proceedings (Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987).

47. That subsequent to the decision passed by the Full Board in Case No.3-108 of 1995 (Review) on 9-12-2003 the respondent No. 6 as petitioner again filed an application before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka for mutation of his name and same was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) after considering all aspects of the case and report of the Kanungo held that since the Rule and stay order passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3229 of 2004 is still in force, there is no scope to consider the prayer of the petitioner and accordingly he rejected the Miscellaneous Case filed by the respondent No.6 on 19-10-2006.

48. It appears that undisputedly the case land of Mouza-Tejkunipara, Police Station Tejgaon, previously Keranigonj appertaining to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot No. 560/669 (Annexure-E) and Satinath Bandapaddhaya alias Sagar Babu was the CS recorded owner. Subsequently, the lands in CS Plot No. 560/669 was finally recorded as SA Khatian No. 605, Plot Nos. 1355/1354/1355/1356/1357/1358/ 1365/1370/1377/1383/1384 and 1385 .(Annexure-E(1) in the names of Satinath Bandapaddhaya.

49. It will be further evident from the Certified Copy of the CS Khatian (Annexure-E), SA record of rights being SA Khatian No. 605(Annexure-E(1) in the name of Satinath Bandapaddhaya, (Mutated) SA Khatian No. 605/1 (Annexure-G) wherein out of 12 SA Plots 7 SA Plots being SA Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355 /1356/1357/1358/ and 1365 of SA Khatian No. 605/1 total area of 5 17 have been recorded in the names of Syed Ahmed, Moqbul Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter by Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78.

50. Annexure G(1) is the certified copy of the Finally Published RS Khatian No. 76, RS Plot Nos. 1617/1618/1619/1620/1621/1670/ 1671 of Mouza-Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka which was recorded in the name of aforesaid 3 persons in respect of the case property. The aforesaid facts have been clearly admitted by the respondent No. 6 and it will be further proved from (Annexure-H) Certified Copy of application (Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987) filed by the respondent No.6 through his constituted Attorney, Md Azharul Islam for Mutation and correction of record under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act impleading Pirjada Abul Kashem, Md Hasnain Siddiqui as Opposite-Parties, wherein it is stated that case property is of Mouza-Tejkunipara, at present Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka.

51. It further evident that in the said Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987, the predecessors of the petitioners, Moqbul Ahmed, Syed Ahmed and Khurshid Jahan Akhter and original SA recorded owner, Satinath Banda-paddhaya were not made parties. Therefore, the order passed in the said Miscellaneous Case on 9-1-1988 by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon (Annexure-H(1) cancelling several Mutation cases including Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and passed order for correcting SA record of right in the name of respondent No. 6-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury in place of SA recorded owner, Satinath Bandapaddhaya without impleading the names of the Satinath and predecessors of the petitioner cannot be binding upon them and the said order is of no avail to the respondent No. 6.

52. Therefore, it is apparent from the record that the petitioner's predecessors got the title of the suit property on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 280 of 1970 on 29-12-1970 against the respondent No.6 and mutated their names in the record of rights by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 9 of 1977-78 and paying rents to the Government.

53. Moreover, during pendency of the Review application before the Land Appeal Board, respondent No. 6-Abdus Sattar Chowdhury made an oral gift to his son Mintu Chowdhury, added respondent No. 6 on 14-3-2002 and in recognition of said oral gift swore an Affidavit on 21-3-2002, and became absolute owner in possession on the basis of the said oral gift. Though added respondent No. 6 became owner of the case land on 14-3-2002 but curiously enough his father, Abdus Satter Chowdhury filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006 for cancellation of the earlier Mutation cases in respect of 12 SA Plot Nos. 1353 /1354/1355/1356/1357/1358/1365/1370/ 1377/1383/1384 of SA Khatian No. 605 and 1385 for an area of 8.70 acres to correct his name in the said SA Khatian No. 605 of Mouza Tejkunipara, at presents Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka.

54. It is pertinent to note that once Revision of Record of Rights was finally published under section 144(7) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SAT Act) and the publication shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under this section. Section 144A lays down that a finally published record of rights prepared or revised under section 144 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act has a presumption of correctness and that presumption continues till it is otherwise rebutted by reliable evidence. In the present case it is evident from Annexure-G (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply that the names of the petitioner's predecessors were finally published in the RS Khatian No. 76, Plot NICS. 1617/1618/1619/ 1620/1621/1670/ 1671 of Mouza-Tejgaon Shilpa Elaka. In such view of the matter, continuation of Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 and decisions passed by the Revenue Officers and the Land Appeal Board become inoperative since RS Khatian No. 76 has finally been published in respect of the case property in the name of the predecessors of the petitioners during continuation of Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987.

55. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the present case and the above legal position, we do not find any merit in the submission of Md Rafiqul Islam that 7 RS Plot Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/1347/1358 and 1365 of RS Khatian No. 605 of Mouza Tejkunipara are not related to same SA Khatian and plots as claimed by the writ petitioners. Actually .those RS 7 plot are SA plots but due to oversight of the learned Advocate for the pre-decessors of the petitioners, those are inadvertently stated as RS Khatian and RS plots is the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 280 of 1870 but those RS plots correspond to CS Khatian No. 211, CS Plot Nos. 560/669 This fact of mistake will be abundantly proved from the Certified Copy of SA Khatian No. 605 and Mutated SA,. Khatian No. 605/1 (Annexure-E and E (1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply) that those 7 Plots are SA Plots Nos. 1353/1354/1355/1356/ 1347/1358/ and 1365 of SA Khatian No. 605 and not RS khatian and RS Plots. Given this scenario, it cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that there was existence of any RS Khatian and RS Plots in the year 1970. In fact RS record of rights was prepared and finally published long after 1970 and during 1975-1990.

56. Further more, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr Anwarul Azim Khair has especially drawn our attention to paragraph No. 4 of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 11-11-2009 wherein it has been stated that by Annexure-1, the writ petitioners want to introduce new facts but in the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 18-5-2010 in paragraph 2 (i) it is stated that Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2006 (Annexure-1) was not filed by the Abdus Satter Chowdhury which was a collusive one. In such situation, we have no option but to hold that those statements made in Paragraph Nos. 4 and 2(i) of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition are deemed to have been admitted by the added respondent No. 6. Having regard to the statements, made in aforementioned paragraphs of the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 11-11-2009 and 18-5-2010 and in consideration of (Annexure-1) dated 19-10-2006, we are led to hold that the instant writ petition is quite competent. So the submissions of Mr Rafiqul Islam on those aspects of the matter stand negative.

<u>57. In the present case, it is an admitted fact that the names of the predecessors of the petitioners have already been recorded in the finally published RS Khatian No. 67(Annexure-G(1) to the Affidavit-in-Reply). In such circumstances, the High Court Division by exercising the power of judicial review under article 102 (2) (a) (ii) of the constitution was competent to inquire into the correctness of the decision if it finds that all the circumstances needed for passing the order were not forthcoming, it will declare the order to be void. In this context, Mr Anwarul Azim Khair has drawn our attention to a decision in a case of Munipal Council, Sujanpur vs Surinder Kumar reported in (2006) 5 SCC 173 wherein it has been stated in paragraph 11:—</u>

<u>"11. The High Court's Jurisdiction to issue a writ of certiorari is limited, a writ of certiorari can be issued if there is an error of law apparent on the face of record. What would constitute an error of law is well known. In judicial Review of Administrative Action. IV the Edition page 136-37, SA desmith has summed up the position:</u>

<u>"(5) The concept of error of law includes the giving of reasons that are bad in law or (if there is a duty to give reasons) inconsistent, unintelligible or, it would seem, substantially inadequate, It includes also the application of a wrong legal test to the facts found, taking irrelevant considerations into account and failing to take relevant considerations into account, exercising a discretion on the basis of any other incorrect legal principles, misdirection as to the burden of proof, and wrongful admission or exclusion of evidence, as well as arriving at a conclusion without any supporting evidence."</u>

<u>(See also SN Chandrashekar vs State of Karnataka, (2006) 3 SCC 208 and Bombay Dyeing and Mfg. Co. Ltd, vs Bombay Environmental Action Group (2006) 3 SCC 434.)</u>

58. Thus, we find that Full Board has misdirected itself as to the question of law involved in the case and reviewed the matter which are not within its jurisdiction as provided under Rule 3(3) of the Land Appeal Board Rules, 1990. We are of the opinion that under circumstances the decision passed in the review of the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board is liable to be interfered by this court as the Full Board travelled beyond its jurisdiction in deciding matters not within its jurisdiction contemplated under the Land Appeal Board Rules, 1990.

59. With reference to the decisions of 8 MLR (AD) 149, 10 MLR (AD) 2005, 47 DLR (AD) 9 and 50 DLR (AD) 213 made by the learned Senior Advocate for the respondent No. 6, we opine that the said decisions, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, have no manner of application. So the reference to the above decisions by Mr Rafiqul Islam does not help him in any way.

60. The impugned order dated 9-12-2003 (Annexure-D to the writ petition) indicate that Full Board without discovery of new and important matter or evidence or any mistake or error on the face of the record or showing any sufficient ground granted review in setting aside the order passed by the Board. In such view of the matter, we find that the Full Board exceeded its jurisdiction under the statute in setting aside the order passed by the Board dated 29-4-1995 in Case No. 3-85 of 1984 (Appeal)-Dhaka (Annexure-C to the writ petition).

61. From the foregoing discussions and having regard to the factual circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the order dated 9-12-2003 passed by the Full Board of the Land Appeal Board in Case No. 3-108 of 1995 (Review) Dhaka allowing the review and revising the decision passed by the Chairman, Land Appeal Board dated 29-8-1995 in Case No. 3-85 of 1994 (Appeal) Dhaka (Annexure-C) and allowing the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1987 are without lawful authority and of no legal effect. The Rule therefore, succeeds.

62. We, therefore, make the rule absolute without any order as to cost. It is declared that impugned order dated 9-12-2003 (Annexure-D) has been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect and the respondent No. 1 is directed to cancel the same and the respondent No. 5 is directed to restore the SA records in the names of the petitioners to the extent of 5.17 acres as it originally stood.

Communicate this Judgment to the Land Appeal Board (respondent No. 1) at once.

End.
